project: kcl/tpipe — TPipe: stream-to-callback adaptor (kcl addition, no FPC source). Runs a producer argv or stdin in the calling shell and hands each record to a callback / array / list, so `producer | obj.method` state loss is designed out.
status: P0 DONE 2026-09-11 (pending commit SHA in the log). tpipe suite 48/48 on bash 5.2.37 and 5.3.9; master sweep 21/21 suites 0 [FAIL] on 5.2.37 and on 5.3.9 (rerun after the F4 race fix). Earlier: Design accepted by the owner 2026-09-10 with defaults D1–D5 (PLAN.md §2.0); D6 chosen by the supervisor and flagged to the owner. Critic pass 2026-09-10: 23 findings (2 BLOCKER, 8 MAJOR, 8 MINOR, 5 NIT), all folded into PLAN.md §1–§6 (record in §8). No code.

decisions.D1: stdin form in a subshell (BASH_SUBSHELL>0) is refused: rc 2, RESULT='', nothing read, kk.debug prints the pinned message (PLAN §2.5) naming the `--` form and `shopt -s lastpipe` in a NON-interactive script
decisions.D2: early stop = explicit TPipe.stop from inside the callback; callback rc ignored; stop flag is a `local` of the sink frame (dynamic scoping), so nested sinks each own their stop
decisions.D4: GNU tools as shipped by MSYS2; no BSD layer (affects tutil)
decisions.D5: TPipe is a kcl unit (kcl/tpipe), not a kkore helper
decisions.D6: SUPERVISOR CHOICE, FLAGGED: the `--` form under BASH_SUBSHELL>0 ($( ), ( ), pipe RHS) also loses instance-callback mutations and nameref fills; it stays ALLOWED with one kk.debug line, because `out=$(TPipe.each fmt -- cmd)` with a plain formatting function is a legitimate stateless use and that subshell is the caller's explicit choice. Owner may flip to rc 2 before P0 starts.

execution_log.summary: Opus worker, supervisor review against the live tree. tpipe.sh (356 lines): guard, locale, tpipe._ret (tpath verbatim), three load-time globals (__TPIPE_STOP=0, __TPIPE_RC=-1, TPIPE_INDEX=0), plain helpers _ret/_pending/_isFunc/_open/_close, TPipe.each/stop/lastRc real, toArray/toList/first/count still _pending stubs (rc 2, RESULT untouched). Red-first against the P0.1 skeleton: 43 FAIL of 47 (001: 32/36, 002: 11/11; the 4 non-red are the harness pin and three rc-2-and-silent halves a stub satisfies by construction). Green: 48/48 on bash 5.2.37 AND 5.3.9 after the two review remarks (a 48th case for the TPIPE_INDEX global, red-first 1 FAIL). Reviewer probes on both bashes: three forms with an instance callback (hits=3 under lastpipe and in the -- form), D1 line byte-exact, IFS=':' around -0 still 2 records, exotic matrix byte-exact, stop on a SIGPIPE-ignoring sleeper in 16-22 ms with lastRc 143, failing producer rc 1 with the count kept, rc 2 leaves a here-string unread, zero forks (BASHPID). Worker findings accepted into PLAN: `declare -F --` is load-bearing (a bare `declare -F '--'` accepts `--` as a callback); the record counter lives in __tpi_n with TPIPE_INDEX as a mirror, so a callback assigning TPIPE_INDEX cannot corrupt RESULT; F4/F5 are exercised via each+stop until `first` lands (P1); the D6 warning text is pinned in §2.5. Master sweep: 5.2.37 21/21 suites 0 [FAIL]; 5.3.9 first run 1 FAIL — F4 pinned lastRc 141 on `yes`, but close → kill -TERM → wait is a race (the TERM landed first under load, 143); PLAN §2.3 already allowed both, the test now accepts 141 or 143 (F5 stays strict: a SIGPIPE-ignoring producer can only die of TERM); 5.3.9 rerun 21/21 0 [FAIL]. Committed as kcl <SHA-P0>.

Owner asked for a way to call an object's method per line of a tool's output (`TGrep.search x | Obj.onLine`) plus a wrapper base. Measured on bash 5.2.37 + 5.3.9: RHS of | loses object state (n=0), `< <()` and lastpipe keep it; BASH_SUBSHELL distinguishes the two; exec {fd}< <(cmd) + wait $pid gives the producer rc; closing the fd kills an infinite producer (141); -d '' NUL records; mapfile -u; nested kklass dispatch keeps the callee's state. Design: TPipe (this unit, five sinks + stop + lastRc, `--` argv form and guarded stdin form) separate from TUtil/TGrep (kcl/tutil/PLAN.md). Owner accepted D1–D5. PLAN.md + this ledger written; no code.

Opus critic, 15 probe scripts on both bashes (scratchpad critic_tpipe/). BLOCKERS: (1) `${d:+-d ''}` in the read header is split by the CALLER's IFS — with IFS=':' the delimiter silently became a space; fixed by passing the delimiter as a value `-d "$d"`. (2) `wait` after closing the fd hangs for the life of a producer that ignores SIGPIPE and stops writing (8.1 s measured); fixed by close → kill -TERM → guarded wait on the stop path (returns in ~50 ms, rc 143; `kill -- -pid` does not work, procsub is not a group leader). MAJORS: global stop flag with reset-on-exit lost an outer stop requested before an inner sink → stop flag is now a `local` of the sink frame (dynamic scoping gives all four nested semantics for free); the `--` form under $( )/( )/pipe RHS also loses instance-callback state → D6 (allowed + debug line, flagged to the owner); rc 1 with non-empty RESULT is a named deviation from kcl §1.2; perf gates re-based on a plain-function callback (instance dispatch is 200/167 µs per record, published not gated); ktests runs threaded ×8 by default → ceilings ≥ 3×, first-latency 250 ms; mapfile into an assoc/readonly target prints a bash diagnostic → rc 2 pre-check; the producer inherits the caller's stdin → documented, tests set their own stdin; bare `wait` aborts a set -e caller → guarded everywhere. MINOR/NIT: lastRc -1 for the stdin form (read PIPESTATUS), NUL-in-record carve-out, blocking producers documented, ForEach citation corrected to onNotify (ForEach is rc 1), word-after-operand rule, D1 message pinned with the job-control caveat, _ret prints in a pipe RHS (tpath contract, documented), red-first is against the P0.1 skeleton (build refuses a bodiless member), producer stderr scoped out of the silence assertion, stop leaves RESULT untouched, kk._outName instance-array refusal is context-dependent, -c kept and explained, record ordinal exposed as TPIPE_INDEX (a frame-local variable, not a second positional — that would break printf-style callbacks). 20+ claims verified correct and listed in PLAN §8 so the worker does not re-probe them.
